label: No Black Lives Matter Movement
detail: The Black Lives Matter movement never emerges, so the 2020 summer protests over policing and race never take place.
assumption: Racial justice and policing are far less salient in the campaign; protest and unrest stories are absent, and the racial justice plank is removed from both platforms. Turnout and vote choice of the electorate otherwise follow their 2020 patterns.
facts_text: No national movement against police killings of Black Americans has formed, and there have been no large street protests over policing this year.
Policing and race relations are not a major subject of the presidential campaign.
research_questions: How did voters' attention to race and policing shift after the large protest waves of 2014 and 2020?
How did white suburban and Black voters change their vote or turnout when policing and unrest dominated the news?
How did the 1968 election respond to urban unrest and the law-and-order appeal?
